story: Fairbanks Ordinance 2026-42, a moratorium on land use permits for large-scale data centers, goes to the Planning Commission on November 10th with staff recommending approval and two amendments

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission meets on November 10th at 6:00 p.m.
claims.verbatim: November 10, 2026 at 6:00 p.m.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (meeting agenda)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch on the live agenda. date_of_source is the meeting date the agenda is written for. The agenda was posted in advance and was retrieved on 2026-11-07 (showrunner curl) and 2026-11-08 (this check), so it was public inside the window.

claims.claim: The meeting is in the Mona Lisa Drexler Assembly Chambers of the Juanita Helms Administration Center at 907 Terminal Street in Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: 907 Terminal Street, Fairbanks, AK
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (meeting agenda)
claims.notes: The same agenda also carries the separate strings "Mona Lisa Drexler Assembly Chambers" and "Juanita Helms Administration Center", both confirmed live.

claims.claim: Ordinance 2026-42, establishing a temporary moratorium on land use permits for large scale data centers, is item G.4 under public hearings on the November 10th agenda.
claims.verbatim: ORDINANCE NO. 2026-42 An Ordinance Establishing A Temporary Moratorium On Land Use Permits For Large Scale Data Centers.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (meeting agenda)
claims.notes: The section heading is "PUBLIC HEARINGS AND LEGISLATIVE HEARINGS" (section G), confirmed live.

claims.claim: Mayor Hopkins sponsors Ordinance 2026-42 and Kellen Spillman is the staff contact.
claims.verbatim: (Sponsor: Mayor Hopkins) (Staff Contact: Kellen Spillman)
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (meeting agenda)
claims.notes: The ordinance header in the packet reads "By: Grier Hopkins, Mayor" (local curl copy, out/2026-11-07/sources/fnsb_pc_packet_13403_tail.txt), which supplies the first name.

claims.claim: Item G.3 on the same agenda is an ordinance adopting a major update of the borough's Regional Comprehensive Plan, sponsored by the Planning Commission.
claims.verbatim: An Ordinance Adopting A Major Update Of The Fairbanks North Star Borough Regional Comprehensive Plan
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (meeting agenda)
claims.notes: Listed as ORDINANCE NO. 2026-TBD, "(Sponsor: Planning Commission)". Staff contacts on the live agenda are Kayde Whiteside, Kellen Spillman and Melissa Kellner (the merge omitted these).

claims.claim: The agenda limits citizens' comments to three minutes.
claims.verbatim: Citizens' Comments - limited to three (3) minutes
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (meeting agenda)
claims.notes: This is agenda item C.2, the general citizens' comments period. The agenda line verified does not state the time limit for testimony on the G.4 public hearing itself. Do not write that hearing testimony on 2026-42 is limited to three minutes; write that the agenda's citizens' comments period is limited to three minutes.

claims.claim: The staff report on Ordinance 2026-42 is from Kellen D. Spillman, Director of the Department of Community Planning.
claims.verbatim: Kellen D. Spillman, Director
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Live WebFetch at offset 746500. The next line reads "Department of Community Planning". TO line is "Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission"; the subject line is labelled SUBJECT. The local curl copy begins mid-header and does not contain the FROM line; the live fetch does. WebFetch measured the packet's plain text at 774,898 characters, not the ~778,600 in the merge; the merge offsets still landed on the right passages, and the difference is consistent with a byte count versus a character count (the text carries curly quotes and ligatures).

claims.claim: The staff report is dated November 10th, the day of the hearing.
claims.verbatim: November 10, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: DATE line of the memo header. The memo is dated forward to the meeting; it was public in the packet by 2026-11-07, when the showrunner saved it.

claims.claim: The staff report says the Assembly referred Ordinance 2026-42 to the Planning Commission on October 26th.
claims.verbatim: Ordinance No. 2026-42 was referred by the FNSB Assembly for Planning Commission recommendation on October 26, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: DISCREPANCY, UNRESOLVED. The ordinance's own header reads "Referred to the Planning Commission: 10/22/2026" (see c10). Both strings are on the same live page. Context, not a resolution: October 22nd, 2026 is a Thursday and October 26th is a Monday; Carousel No.94, published October 23rd, already covered the referral, which sits more easily with October 22nd. The deck should not state a single referral date as fact. Safe phrasing is "referred in late October", or cite both.

claims.claim: The ordinance's header records its referral to the Planning Commission as October 22nd.
claims.verbatim: Referred to the Planning Commission: 10/22/2026
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly (Ordinance No. 2026-42, Attachment A in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Contradicts the staff report's October 26th (c09). Recorded separately on purpose. On the page the header text is laid out across numbered lines 2 and 3 ("Referred to the" / "Planning Commission:  10/22/2026"). The ordinance page footers read "ORDINANCE NO. 2026-XX" while the title block reads 2026-42, a clerical inconsistency inside the attachment.

claims.claim: The staff report describes the moratorium as pausing action on land use permits for large-scale data centers for approximately one year, to the end of 2027.
claims.verbatim: for approximately one year (end of 2027)
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Full sentence on the page: "The attached ordinance puts forth a moratorium, essentially pausing action on any land use permits, for "large-scale data centers" for approximately one year (end of 2027)." Cross-check: consistent with Section 3's December 31, 2027 end (c34) and with "until 2028" (c24). The span is about one year only if the ordinance is adopted around the end of 2026; it would be shorter for a later adoption.

claims.claim: The Community Planning Department supports the ordinance as time to research, draft regulations and run a public process.
claims.verbatim: The Community Planning Department is supportive of this ordinance to allow additional time to research, develop draft regulations and engage in a public process.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Confirmed live and in the local copy.

claims.claim: The staff report says data centers have become the most highly commented-on topic of the ongoing comprehensive plan update.
claims.verbatim: they have become the most highly commented-on topic of the ongoing update to the plan
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: The phrase spans a page break in the packet: "most highly" ends packet page 1154 and "commented-on topic" opens page 1155, with a footnote and the page footer between. Joined wording confirmed live. No comment count is given.

claims.claim: Commenters raised water and air quality, power and water supply, noise, vibrations and size among their concerns.
claims.value: water, air, power, noise, vibrations and size
claims.verbatim: Commenters have expressed concern about and the desire to regulate impacts to water and air quality, impacts to the power and water supply, noise, vibrations and size, among other impacts.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: This is staff's summary of public comment, not a finding that these impacts occur. Attribute: "according to the staff report, commenters raised...".

claims.claim: The borough zoning code has no definition for data center.
claims.verbatim: There is currently no definition for data center in the FNSB zoning code.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Corroborated inside the ordinance WHEREAS clause: "the Borough zoning code does not address data centers as a permitted or conditional use".

claims.claim: Data centers are not listed as a permitted or conditional use in any borough zone, and there are no supplemental standards for their impacts.
claims.verbatim: It is not listed as a permitted or conditional use in any zone, and there are no supplemental standards to regulate the unique impacts of this use.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Read with care beside the ordinance's WHEREAS clause, verified in No.94 and present in this packet: "large-scale data centers would be permitted only in the GU-1 and GU-5 General Use Districts". The two documents agree once you see that the General Use districts "allow for the widest range of land uses". Data centers are not named in any zone, but these catch-all districts would let them in. Do not write "banned everywhere" or "allowed nowhere".

claims.claim: Warehouse is an undefined use permitted or conditional in the General Commercial, Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial zones.
claims.verbatim: "Warehouse" is an undefined use listed as a permitted or conditional use in the General Commercial, Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial zones.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: The page has curly quotes around Warehouse, normalized to straight. The next sentence adds that the use "may be similar to a data center, though it does not include the same unique impacts".

claims.claim: Under Title 18 a large scale development includes a retail or wholesale building over 55,000 square feet of gross floor area.
claims.verbatim: individually or cumulatively, exceed(s) 55,000 square feet of gross floor area
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Staff quotes the FNSBC 18.04.010 definition (footnote 4). Limb (1) opens "A retail or wholesale building or buildings, located on a zoning lot". Measured against the code text as quoted in the staff report, not the live municipal code.

claims.claim: Title 18 also defines a large scale development as an entertainment facility over 40,000 square feet seating 800 or more people.
claims.verbatim: An entertainment facility exceeding 40,000 square feet and which has a seating capacity of 800 people or more.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Two figures, both on the same line: 40,000 square feet AND 800 seats, and both must be met. The proposed 40,000 square foot data center trigger (c29) lines up with this entertainment limb, not with the 55,000 square foot retail limb.

claims.claim: Large scale developments have Title 18 standards for building aesthetics, maintenance and parking lot design.
claims.verbatim: Large scale developments have standards in Title 18 to address building aesthetics, maintenance, and parking lot design.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Confirmed live at offset 752800.

claims.claim: Staff cites a 2014 statewide ballot initiative that legalized marijuana facilities as a precedent.
claims.verbatim: In 2014, a statewide ballot initiative legalized marijuana facilities
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Same paragraph: "The FNSB went through a very similar process in 2014 and 2015 regarding legalized marijuana facilities" and no municipality had a zoning code set up for them. Staff cites FNSB Ordinance 2015-41 (footnote 5).

claims.claim: The state marijuana licensing process took about 18 months from the vote to the first license and acted as a de facto moratorium, according to staff.
claims.verbatim: took about 18 months from the vote to when the first license was approved. This licensing process essentially acted as a de facto moratorium
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Staff's own approximation, and the claim keeps "about" and "according to staff". The timeline was not independently re-verified against state licensing records this run.

claims.claim: The staff report names the Municipality of Anchorage among places that have researched and passed data center regulations.
claims.verbatim: There are many municipalities in the United States and even Alaska that have researched and passed regulations regarding data centers, including the Municipality of Anchorage.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Verified only as Fairbanks staff's statement. Anchorage's own regulation was not fetched or checked this run, so its content, date and ordinance number are unknown here. Phrase it as "according to Fairbanks borough staff, Anchorage has passed data center regulations".

claims.claim: Staff writes that the ordinance would pause any large-scale data center development until 2028 or until regulations are adopted.
claims.verbatim: This ordinance would pause any development of a large-scale data center until 2028 or when regulations are adopted.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: This is staff's paraphrase. The ordinance text itself (c34) runs "through December 31, 2027, unless terminated sooner or extended by ordinance of the Assembly", and it contains no automatic end when regulations are adopted. Early termination takes an Assembly ordinance. For the operative terms, prefer the ordinance wording. Also note the ordinance blocks land use permit applications, not "any development" in every sense.

claims.claim: Staff says the ordinance sets a six month timeline for Community Planning to report to the Planning Commission.
claims.verbatim: this would set a timeline of six months for the Community Planning Department to present a report to the Planning Commission.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Matches ordinance Section 4 (c36): "within six months of the effective date of this ordinance".

claims.claim: The Community Planning Department has received inquiries about data centers potentially being developed in the borough.
claims.verbatim: There have been inquiries received by the FNSB Community Planning Department on data centers potentially being developed in the community.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: No count, no names, no sizes, no applications. Do not turn this into "proposals" or "applications". It says inquiries about data centers that might be developed.

claims.claim: Staff recommends two amendments because large-scale developments and large-scale data centers are expected to be of similar size and impact.
claims.verbatim: because large-scale developments and large-scale data centers are anticipated to be of similar size and have similar impacts, Community Planning recommends the following two amendments to provide uniform oversight.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: The sentence opens "For the time being,". The executive summary also describes the amendments as meant "to better align "large-scale data centers" with other somewhat like uses in code".

claims.claim: The first amendment adds the word gross before floor area in the data center definition.
claims.verbatim: Amend line 59 to add "gross" before "floor area."
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Curly quotes normalized to straight. LINE NUMBER DISCREPANCY: in the ordinance as printed in this packet, "floor area" falls on numbered line 60 ("megawatts (5 MW) or greater; or (2) occupies more than 50,000 square feet of floor area"). Line 59 reads "transmission of digital data that: (1) has an aggregate peak electrical demand of five". So the staff amendment's "line 59" is off by one against the packet copy. This was measured on the local curl copy of the same URL, and the live fetch confirmed the amendment text but not the line numbering. Harmless to the substance, but don't print line numbers in the deck.

claims.claim: The second amendment lowers the floor area trigger from 50,000 to 40,000 square feet.
claims.verbatim: Amend line 60 to change 50,000 square feet to 40,000 square feet.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Arithmetic re-derived: 50,000 minus 40,000 is 10,000 square feet, a 20 percent cut in the threshold. 40,000 matches the entertainment facility limb of large scale development (c19), not the 55,000 retail or wholesale limb (c18). If the deck says the amendment aligns data centers with large scale development, say it matches the 40,000 square foot entertainment threshold. Combined with c28 the amended trigger would read more than 40,000 square feet of gross floor area.

claims.claim: The Community Planning Department recommends approval of Ordinance 2026-42 with the two amendments.
claims.verbatim: The Community Planning Department recommends approval of Ordinance 2026-42 with said amendments.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: The packet also carries a draft motion: "I move to recommend adoption of Ordinance No. 2026-42" plus the two amendment motions. This is a recommendation to the Planning Commission. No vote has happened yet, so don't describe one.

claims.claim: The ordinance's first trigger is an aggregate peak electrical demand of 5 MW or more.
claims.verbatim: has an aggregate peak electrical demand of five megawatts (5 MW) or greater
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly (Ordinance No. 2026-42, Attachment A in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Section 2. The three triggers are joined by "or", so meeting any one makes a facility a large-scale data center. Already reported in No.94 and repeated here as background. The staff report restates it as "(5MW)".

claims.claim: The ordinance's second trigger is more than 50,000 square feet of floor area devoted to data center operations.
claims.verbatim: occupies more than 50,000 square feet of floor area devoted to data center operations
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly (Ordinance No. 2026-42, Attachment A in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: This is the figure the c29 amendment would change to 40,000. The text breaks across numbered lines 60 and 61.

claims.claim: The ordinance's third trigger is onsite electrical generation with a capacity of 5 MW or more.
claims.verbatim: includes onsite electrical generation facilities with a generating capacity of five megawatts (5 MW) or greater
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly (Ordinance No. 2026-42, Attachment A in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Confirmed live at offset 752800 and in the local copy.

claims.claim: Section 3 keeps the moratorium in effect through December 31st, 2027, unless the Assembly ends or extends it by ordinance.
claims.verbatim: shall be in effect through December 31, 2027, unless terminated sooner or extended by ordinance of the Assembly.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly (Ordinance No. 2026-42, Attachment A in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Confirmed live at offset 761800. Section 5 makes the ordinance effective "at 5:00 p.m." on "the first Borough business day following its adoption". Section 2 bars accepting new land use permit applications for a large-scale data center and approving pending ones.

claims.claim: Section 4 directs a study of data center impacts on energy usage, air quality, water usage and water quality, and noise pollution.
claims.verbatim: including but not limited to impacts on energy usage, air quality, water usage and water quality, and noise pollution.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly (Ordinance No. 2026-42, Attachment A in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: The Department of Community Planning does the study. The list is open-ended ("including but not limited to").

claims.claim: Section 4 requires the study report and recommendations within six months of the ordinance taking effect.
claims.verbatim: for the land use regulation of large-scale data centers within six months of the effective date of this ordinance.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly (Ordinance No. 2026-42, Attachment A in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: The report goes to the Planning Commission. Corroborates staff's c25.

claims.claim: The ordinance states the borough's Regional Comprehensive Plan was last updated in 2005.
claims.verbatim: was last updated in 2005, prior to growing demand from artificial intelligence
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly (Ordinance No. 2026-42, Attachment A in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: First WHEREAS clause. Corroborated in the staff report: "the existing Comprehensive Plan was adopted in 2005".

claims.claim: The ordinance says the comprehensive plan update is expected to be finalized in early 2027.
claims.verbatim: expected to be finalized in early 2027
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly (Ordinance No. 2026-42, Attachment A in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: A projection. Keep "expected". On the page the phrase breaks across numbered lines 25 and 26 ("is still in progress and expected" / "to be finalized in early 2027").

claims.claim: The comprehensive plan draft describes data centers as industrial warehouse-type facilities that have long made up the physical infrastructure of the internet.
claims.verbatim: Data centers are industrial warehouse-type facilities that have long made up the physical infrastructure of the internet.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (Regional Comprehensive Plan, Planning Commission Draft, in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Section "Data Centers and the FNSB Comprehensive Plan", Chapter 3 (Land Use, Housing, and Small Area Planning), plan page 46, packet page 165 of 1162. One fetch first read it as page 45; a targeted re-fetch of the page markers put it on page 46 (the "Page | 45" footer closes the previous page), which matches the merge. This is a draft and could still change.

claims.claim: The draft says data centers can produce more noise than comparable warehouse facilities and could affect local power and water infrastructure.
claims.verbatim: produce more noise than comparable warehouse facilities.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (Regional Comprehensive Plan, Planning Commission Draft, in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: The sentence opens "These facilities have the potential to impact local power and water infrastructure" (confirmed live as a separate fragment). The draft frames it as potential, so keep "can" or "could" and don't state it as a measured Fairbanks effect.

claims.claim: The draft quotes the American Planning Association noting that data centers get slotted into broad zoning buckets even though they are packed wall-to-wall with servers instead of pallets.
claims.verbatim: even though the buildings may be packed wall-to-wall with servers instead of pallets.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (Regional Comprehensive Plan, Planning Commission Draft, in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Footnote 1 attributes it to American Planning Association, 2025, "Zoning Practice: The Physical Footprint of Artificial Intelligence." Earlier in the same quote: "Where definitions are absent, planners may choose to slot these facilities into broad buckets" (confirmed live). The intervening words, which per WebFetch's paraphrase name categories like warehousing, light industrial or public utility, were NOT obtained verbatim, so don't quote them. The APA original was not fetched. Attribute as "quoted in the borough's draft plan", not as a quote checked against APA. The staff report's footnote 6 also lists "The Physical Footprint of Artificial Intelligence" from Zoning Practice, which corroborates the citation.

claims.claim: The draft says data centers have drawn interest in Alaska because the favorable ambient air temperature for cooling gives developers a significant advantage.
claims.verbatim: Data centers have gained public interest in Alaska, due to the favorable ambient air temperature for cooling
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (Regional Comprehensive Plan, Planning Commission Draft, in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: The sentence continues "which offers a significant advantage for project developers." (confirmed live). The draft says "favorable ambient air temperature" and never "cold". Paraphrasing as cold air is fair in meaning but isn't the draft's word, so don't put "cold" inside quotation marks.

claims.claim: The draft describes a process in which the Planning Commission recommends to the Assembly and the Assembly holds its own public hearing several weeks later.
claims.verbatim: Several weeks later, the Assembly holds its own public hearing
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (Regional Comprehensive Plan, Planning Commission Draft, in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: From the draft's general "Code Revision Process" description. It continues "where the public may again participate and speak on the ordinance". The preceding sentence reads "The Planning Commission reviews the staff recommendation, consistency with FNSB planning documents," ... "and considers public testimony before making a recommendation to the Assembly." This describes the usual process and is not a scheduled date for 2026-42. No Assembly hearing date for 2026-42 was found. Write "typically" or "under the borough's usual process", not that the Assembly will hear it on any given date.

claims.claim: Draft Strategy 73B proposes using the conditional use permit process as an interim way to permit undefined uses until the zoning code has definitions and standards.
claims.verbatim: Consider using the conditional use permit process as an interim method to permit undefined uses
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (Regional Comprehensive Plan, Planning Commission Draft, in Planning Commission packet)
claims.notes: Plan page 113 (packet page 233), Natural Resources and Environment, Goal A. It continues "prior to the development of definitions and standards in the zoning code." 73B does NOT name data centers. It covers undefined uses in general. Data centers are named in the neighbouring Strategy 73A ("Update the zoning code regarding new technologies and industries such as:" followed by a list ending in "Data centers") and again in Strategy 98D (page 127). Don't call 73B a data center strategy. Say the draft proposes interim conditional use permits for undefined uses, a category that currently includes data centers.

claims.claim: A Fairbanks town hall on data centers took place on October 29th at the Wedgewood Resort.
claims.verbatim: On October 29, nearly 200 people gathered in person at Wedgewood Resort in Fairbanks.
claims.source_outlet: Northern Alaska Environmental Center
claims.notes: Date and venue corroborated independently by Alaska's News Source (KTUU), which says "Thursday night at the Wedgewood Resort" in a story published October 30th. October 29th, 2026 is a Thursday (re-derived). Northern Center is a co-organizer, so this is an advocacy source; the date and venue are not in dispute. Neither source mentions Ordinance 2026-42, the moratorium or the Planning Commission. Tying the town hall to the ordinance is the deck's framing, not the sources'.

claims.claim: Alaska's News Source reported that about 150 Fairbanks residents attended the town hall.
claims.verbatim: About 150 Fairbanks residents gathered Thursday night at the Wedgewood Resort
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: Page reads "Published: Oct. 30, 2026 at 8:00 PM AKDT", byline Alex Bengel. The URL path says 2026/10/31, which is a URL artifact; use October 30th. This is a reporter's estimate. Attribute it, and present it next to the organizer figure (c47) rather than picking one.

claims.claim: The Northern Alaska Environmental Center, a co-organizer, says nearly 200 people attended in person.
claims.verbatim: nearly 200 people gathered in person
claims.source_outlet: Northern Alaska Environmental Center
claims.notes: This is the organizer's own count, and it differs from KTUU's "About 150". It must be attributed ("organizers say"). Northern Center credits itself and Alaskans for Data Center Accountability (AFDCA), with AKPIRG, ACAT, The Alaska Center Education Fund, Native Movement and Families Over Billionaires thanked as helping.

claims.claim: Organizers say more than 100 additional viewers joined the town hall through online livestreams.
claims.verbatim: more than 100 additional viewers joining through online livestreams
claims.source_outlet: Northern Alaska Environmental Center
claims.notes: Organizer figure, single source, no independent corroboration. The same page totals it as "More than 300 Alaskans joined the conversation in Fairbanks." Use only with attribution.

claims.claim: Sarah Hollister, who helped organize the town hall, said our largest concern is that nobody asked us.
claims.verbatim: Our largest concern is that nobody asked us.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: KTUU identifies her as "Concerned resident Sarah Hollister, who helped to organize the event." It gives no other title or affiliation, so don't invent one. Quote appears verbatim on the fetched page.

claims.claim: Alaska's News Source reported that legislators Scott Kawasaki, Maxine Dibert, Mike Prax and David Guttenberg were among the attendees.
claims.verbatim: Local and state legislators were counted among the attendees, including Scott Kawasaki, Maxine Dibert, Mike Prax and David Guttenberg.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: "including" means these four are named and others may have attended. The page gives no offices, chambers, districts or positions for them, and none were verified here. Attending isn't endorsing; don't imply a stance.

claims.claim: The town hall was billed as Nobody Asked Us, an Alaska town hall about data centers, AI and tax dollars.
claims.verbatim: Nobody Asked Us: An Alaska Town Hall About Data Centers, AI, and Our Tax Dollars.
claims.source_outlet: Northern Alaska Environmental Center
claims.notes: The event title is the organizer's own wording, and the source is fit for that. It echoes Hollister's quote (c49).

claims.claim: The University of Alaska Board of Regents met in Fairbanks on November 4th to 6th on the UAF campus.
claims.verbatim: will meet in Fairbanks, November 4-6, on the University of Alaska Fairbanks (UAF) campus
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska System
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP story. Fetched through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.alaska.edu/news/system/2026-ua-board-of-regents-november-board-meeting.php because alaska.edu returns 503 to WebFetch directly. The release is dated November 3rd and is a preview ("will meet"), so it doesn't prove the meeting ran as planned.

claims.claim: Chief Information Technology Officer Ben Shier was scheduled to share the latest version of UA's AI Engaged effort with the regents.
claims.verbatim: Chief Information Technology Officer Ben Shier will share the latest version of UA's "AI Engaged" effort.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska System
claims.notes: Curly quotes and apostrophe normalized to straight. A preview, so write "was scheduled to". No vote outcome or presentation record was found.

claims.claim: AI Engaged establishes six guiding principles, four investment priorities and five system-wide expectations.
claims.verbatim: establishes six guiding principles, four investment priorities and five system-wide expectations
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska System
claims.notes: Per the release, it sets system-level direction while each university keeps responsibility for curriculum, academic integrity and faculty instructional judgment (paraphrased by WebFetch, not verbatim).

claims.claim: In May the Board of Regents directed UA leadership to develop a cohesive strategy for the university's approach to AI.
claims.verbatim: In May, the Board directed UA leadership to develop a cohesive strategy around the university's approach
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska System
claims.notes: Apostrophe normalized. The release goes on to say the strategy should address artificial intelligence from philosophical, pedagogical and operational angles (WebFetch paraphrase, so don't quote it).

claims.claim: Two UAA associate professors wrote in the Anchorage Daily News that Anthropic's Claude generated the initial draft of UA's AI plan.
claims.verbatim: Anthropic's Claude generated the initial draft, a fact concealed for months until Oct. 9.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)
claims.notes: OPINION AND CONTESTED. Verified only as what the op-ed says. The authors are "associate professors at the University of Alaska Anchorage". The page is dated November 4th although the URL path says 11/03. "Concealed" is disputed by a faculty reply (c57), so keep the attribution ("two UAA professors allege") and run the reply next to it.

claims.claim: Five UA faculty replied in the Anchorage Daily News that AI use in drafting the plan was not concealed.
claims.verbatim: In this case, AI use was not "concealed."
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Carroll, Cason, Ryan, Harnish and Trochim)
claims.notes: OPINION. Authors are Jennifer Carroll (UAF), Jackie Cason (UAA), James Ryan (UAS), Andrew Harnish (UAA) and Erin Trochim (UAF Institute of Northern Engineering). They also write "Eventually adding a small AI attribution was a good move", which implicitly concedes the attribution came late. Quote marks normalized to straight.

stories_surviving: Fairbanks Ordinance 2026-42, data center moratorium at the Planning Commission November 10th (44 verified primary claims, c01 to c44)
Fairbanks October 29th data center town hall, secondary to the lead (7 verified claims, c45 to c51, all secondary sources, attendance hedged)
University of Alaska AI Engaged at the November regents meeting, runner-up (4 primary claims c52 to c55, plus 2 attributed opinion claims c56 and c57)

killed.claim: The Planning Commission or the Assembly has voted on Ordinance 2026-42.
killed.why: No vote has happened. The hearing is November 10th, after the run date, and the packet holds only a staff recommendation and a draft motion.

killed.claim: The Assembly will hold its public hearing on Ordinance 2026-42 on a specific date.
killed.why: No Assembly hearing date was found. The draft plan's "Several weeks later" describes the usual process, not a schedule for 2026-42 (see c43).

killed.claim: Public hearing testimony on Ordinance 2026-42 is limited to three minutes per speaker.
killed.why: The verified three-minute line is agenda item C.2, Citizens' Comments. No time limit for the G.4 hearing testimony was verified.

killed.claim: The draft plan cites Alaska's cold air as an advantage for data centers.
killed.why: Wording not on the page. The draft says "favorable ambient air temperature for cooling". The fact survives as c42 in the draft's own words, and "cold" must not appear in quotation marks.

killed.claim: Strategy 73B is a data center specific interim conditional use permit strategy.
killed.why: 73B covers undefined uses in general and doesn't name data centers. Data centers are named in Strategy 73A and 98D. Survives in corrected form as c44.

killed.claim: The APA servers-instead-of-pallets quotation is verified against the American Planning Association's own publication.
killed.why: The APA source wasn't fetched. The quote is verified only as it appears in the borough draft with its footnote (c41). The middle of the quotation, which names the zoning categories, wasn't obtained verbatim and must not be quoted.

killed.claim: The Ordinance 2026-42 referral date is a single settled date.
killed.why: The primary documents conflict. The staff report says October 26, 2026 and the ordinance header says 10/22/2026. Both are recorded (c09, c10) and the conflict is left unresolved by design.

killed.claim: Details of the Municipality of Anchorage's data center regulations, such as ordinance number, date or content.
killed.why: Not fetched. Only the Fairbanks staff report's statement that Anchorage passed regulations is verified (c23).

killed.claim: The October 29th town hall was organized around or responded to Ordinance 2026-42.
killed.why: Neither KTUU nor the Northern Center page mentions the ordinance, the moratorium or the Planning Commission.

killed.claim: Offices or districts for Kawasaki, Dibert, Prax and Guttenberg.
killed.why: The KTUU page names them as "Local and state legislators" without offices. Nothing else was fetched to confirm their titles.

killed.claim: The UA regents voted on, adopted or approved AI Engaged.
killed.why: Outcome not found. The UA release is a November 3rd preview ("will share").

killed.claim: The data center section of the comprehensive plan draft is on plan page 45.
killed.why: A first fetch said page 45, but a targeted re-fetch of the page markers placed it on plan page 46 (packet page 165). Recorded as page 46 in c39.

killed.claim: MEA, Enstar and Hilcorp gas exchange agreement.
killed.why: Not checked. Skipped by instruction (fourth priority, no spare capacity spent). Nothing from it may be used.
